page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-standard-8 is a network-optimized instance powered by the x86_64 Intel Xeon 8581C processor clocked at 2.3 GHz. The configuration allocates 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped across 4 physical cores with 2 threads per core, backed by 30.0 GB of memory (3.75 GB per vCPU). The underlying processor features an extensive instruction set including AVX-512, AMX (tile and int8), and hardware cryptography extensions such as AES, VAES, and SHA-NI, along with 260 MB of L3 cache. The instance includes no bundled local storage and features zero GPUs, requiring remote block storage for persistent operations.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-threaded CPU capabilities alongside balanced multi-core metrics. In single-core evaluations, the instance achieved a top-tier Geekbench single-core score of 2256.0 and scored in the top tier for text processing (2977.0). Decompression and compression benchmarks reflect solid performance, with single-threaded gzip reaching 35.04 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression logging 15.25 GB/sec, placing both in the top 25%. Multi-core throughput aligns with the mid-tier category, showing 8502.0 in Geekbench multi-core, 8882.75 in stress-ng multi-core, and a PassMark CPU score of 15872.98.

In memory and workload-level benchmarks, uncached read and write bandwidths reached 61.57 GB/sec and 36.0 GB/sec, respectively. In-memory data structures handled 12.12 million Redis SET operations per second, while static web serving throughput reached 16.99 GB/sec. When evaluating lightweight language model inference, the small 135M model achieved a top-tier text generation rate of 352.64 tokens/sec, though scaling up to a 7B model dropped text generation into the bottom 25% at 7.21 tokens/sec.

With a 3.75 GB RAM-per-vCPU distribution and balanced multi-core performance, the c4n-standard-8 is tailored for general cloud workloads, network-centric middle-tier applications, API servers, and lightweight CPU-based microservice architectures that do not depend on integrated local disks or accelerated hardware.
